source: Albrechtsberger, in Mann, The Study of Fugue (1958), p. 237, Ex. 218: 'Canon for four voices', at the unison, 'Turnus descendet ad inferos'
transcription: C major: degree 0 = C4 (MIDI 60). Durations in beats, quarter = 1, bar = 4 (common time). Four one-bar sections, the section sign over each bar: each voice enters a bar after the last, and the tune repeats. Bar 4 is E4 and a half rest. Read from the 600 dpi scan with the staff lines measured, and settled by the harmony where a half note's head was ambiguous: every section sounds at once, so beats 1-2 must be consonant (C5 E5 C5 over E4 or C4: C major) and beats 3-4 are G major (D5 B4 G4). The other reading of bars 1-3 (D5 F5 D5) makes sevenths and ninths against Ex. 219's added section.
